after: ## The quantities and how they connect
alt: Current (charge per second, in amperes) times p.d. (energy per coulomb, in volts) gives power (energy per second, in watts), so P = IV; multiplying by time gives E = IVt. For Extended: I = Q/t, V = W/Q and one volt is one joule per coulomb.
caption: Charge per second × energy per coulomb = energy per second.

alt: Before rubbing, an insulating rod and a cloth each hold equal positive and negative charge. Rubbing moves electrons only: the material that gains electrons becomes negative and the one that loses them becomes positive. Below, like charges repel and unlike charges attract.
caption: Electrons move from one material to the other; positive charges stay put.

alt: Field lines point radially outwards from a positive point charge and inwards to a negative one. A charged conducting sphere has radial lines starting at its surface, at right angles to it. Between oppositely charged parallel plates the lines are straight, parallel and evenly spaced, from the positive to the negative plate.
caption: Field direction is the direction of the force on a positive charge.

alt: A battery, an ammeter in series and a lamp with a voltmeter connected across it. The ammeter reads 0.50 A and the voltmeter 6.0 V, so R = 6.0 / 0.50 = 12 Ω. Conventional current is drawn from + to −, while electrons move from − to +.
caption: Ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel, then R = V/I.

alt: A 2.0 m wire of area 0.50 mm² has resistance 3.4 Ω. Making it 5.0 m long multiplies R by 2.5 to 8.5 Ω; doubling the area to 1.0 mm² halves it to 4.25 Ω, about 4.3 Ω.
caption: Apply each change as its own scale factor: length directly, area inversely.

alt: Three sketch I–V graphs with current on the vertical axis. A resistor gives a straight line through the origin. A filament lamp gives a curve through the origin that gets less steep at higher p.d., in both directions. A diode passes almost no current in reverse and, forwards, almost none until a small threshold p.d., then the current rises steeply.
caption: With I on the vertical axis, steeper means lower resistance.

alt: A 2.2 kW kettle on 230 V draws 2200 / 230 = 9.6 A. Over 3.0 minutes it transfers 2200 × 180 = 396 000 J; in kilowatt-hours that is 2.2 × 0.050 = 0.11 kW h, costing 0.11 × 28 = 3.1 cents at 28 cents per kW h.
caption: Use watts and seconds for joules; kilowatts and hours for kW h.
